beliefs: The first character is shifted backward by 2 in the alphabet (a->y, b->z, ..., z->x; A->Y, ..., Z->X) [E7, E8, E9, E10]
All characters after the first are left unchanged, including letters, digits, spaces, and symbols [E1, E4, E5, E6, E7, E8]
If the first character is not a letter (digit, space, symbol, control char, emoji), it is left unchanged [E1, E11, E12]

Non-ASCII letters are shifted backward by 2 in Unicode code point order, wrapping within the contiguous same-case letter block (é->ç, É->Ç, ü->ú, ñ->ï, ø->ö, æ->ä, œ->ő, ß->Ý, à->Þ, þ->ü) [E11, E12, E13, E14]

The shift for non-ASCII letters uses code-point arithmetic within the contiguous run of same-case letters containing the character, not alphabet position; ß (U+00DF) is treated as part of the lowercase run ending at ÿ, so ß->Ý wraps across the × boundary [E12, E13, E14]
The lowercase non-ASCII run starts at à (U+00E0), not at ß; à->Þ wraps backward past ß into the uppercase Þ [E14]
notes: E14 shows à->Þ (wrapping backward past ß to Þ), so the lowercase run begins at à, not ß; and ß->Ý confirms ß is inside the run (index 0, wraps to the end ÿ... but observed Ý). Actually ß->Ý means ß is at index 1 in a run that starts at à? No—need to reconsider: run à..ÿ with ß included gives ß at index 1, -2 wraps to end = ÿ, not Ý. So the run must be ß..ÿ for ß but à..ÿ for à. The simplest consistent rule: shift by -2 code points, and if the result falls in the × gap (U+00D7) or below à, wrap to the end of the lowercase run (ÿ, þ, ...). ß-2=Ý (U+00DD, uppercase, not in lowercase run) — so ß is special: ß->Ý. I'll model ß as its own case: ß-2 code points = U+00DD = Ý directly, no wrapping needed. And à-2=Þ (U+00DE) directly. So plain -2 code point arithmetic works for all of these! ß(U+00DF)-2=U+00DD=Ý ✓, à(U+00E0)-2=U+00DE=Þ ✓, ø-2=ö ✓, æ-2=ä ✓, œ-2=ő ✓, ÿ-2=ý ✓, þ-2=ü ✓. The earlier failures were from my run-wrapping logic; plain -2 code points explains everything.
